title: Lean 4 formalization of Lavi's proof of Foregger's conjecture, conditional on Gurvits's capacity inequality
description:
A sorry-free Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Sections 2–7 of Y. Lavi, Foregger's Conjecture on Minimum Permanents of Nearly Decomposable Doubly Stochastic Matrices (preprint, 2026). It ends with the paper's Theorem 1.1 (lavi_theorem_1_1): for n ≥ 2 and a doubly stochastic matrix A with nearly decomposable support, per A ≥ 2^(1−n), with equality exactly for (1/2)(I + P) up to independent row and column permutations, and strictness on every noncycle nearly decomposable face.

Conditional result. Theorem 1.1 is proved from one explicit hypothesis that is assumed and not proved here: Gurvits's degree-sensitive capacity inequality for permanents (L. Gurvits, Electron. J. Combin. 15 (2008), Theorem 2.4 and Corollary 2.7(a); M. Laurent and A. Schrijver, Amer. Math. Monthly 117 (2010), Corollary 1a). It is a hypothesis of the theorems that use it, not a Lean axiom. This record is therefore a machine-checked reduction of Theorem 1.1 to that inequality, not a complete machine-checked proof of Foregger's conjecture.

The main theorems depend only on Lean's standard axioms (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound), and the files contain no sorry, admit, axiom or native_decide. The Lean statements were translated from the paper with AI assistance and have not yet been independently reviewed by a second person.

The formalization also records simplifications of several arguments, listed in the README (for example Lemma 3.1 without Lagrange multipliers or Sinkhorn scaling, the removability rule (4.3) by a strict-Hall computation, the secant bounds (5.10) by Bernoulli's inequality, and an equality argument that avoids the edge count).

The Lean code was developed with AI coding assistants (Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's Codex), working under the author's direction. Lean's kernel checks every proof.
